summary: Same pattern — identical block/sawtooth-ramp vocabulary, palette and cycle envelope, phase-aligned at t=0 — but the port's whole animation runs 1.67x too fast (3.93 s cycle vs the original's 6.55 s) and it adds a ~0.8 s brightness ripple that occasionally blows the whole strip out to near-white, which the original never does.
observations: Both sides render cleanly on the default rig (strip, 60 px), no compile or runtime errors, neither side binds sensors, and both are fully deterministic — a --seed 7 run (label seed7) reproduces the seed-1 stats exactly on both sides, so nothing here is RNG-driven.

Shared visual vocabulary: the strip carries trains of sawtooth ramps (dark->bright, hue sweeping R->Y->G->C->B->M) whose spatial period changes continuously over time, and the strip is split into two ~30 px blocks that light and darken semi-independently — e.g. at t=15.05 s the original's ramp resets sit only at pixels 32,34,...,58 (right block, 2 px period) while the left block is flat. The port shows the same left/right block behaviour at the same kind of moments.

Both sides are strictly periodic. Autocorrelation of meanBrightness over a 120 s / 20 fps run (label long120) peaks at exactly 131 frames and every multiple for the original (6.55 s cycle, corr ~0.88 out to lag 1179) and at 78.6 frames and multiples for the port (3.93 s cycle, corr ~0.87). Ratio 131/78.6 = 1.667 — the port's master clock is 5/3 too fast. The motion stat agrees: orig avg 13.2 vs port 22.3 at 20 fps (1.69x), and the same ~1.7x gap holds in every window checked (win-20, win-40, win-60).

Both sides are time-based, not frame-stepped: the cycle period measured in SECONDS is unchanged at --fps 10, 20 and 40 (orig 6.55 s at all three; port 3.93 s at all three), so there is no frame-rate-coupling bug on either side.

Cycle SHAPE matches. Folding each side's 120 s meanBrightness/meanR/meanG/meanB onto its own period (32 phase bins) and cross-correlating gives a best phase shift of 0 — the two cycles are already aligned — with brightness corr 0.74 and per-channel envelopes that track closely (e.g. meanB orig 19,60,55,43,21,12,15,18,21,27,32,38,42,40,22,13 vs port 12,68,80,61,20,10,12,14,17,23,30,35,34,22,22,13 over the first half of the cycle).

Speed-compensated waterfalls confirm it visually: rendering exactly two original cycles (cyc-orig, 13.11 s @ 20 fps) against exactly two port cycles (cyc-port, 7.865 s @ 33 fps) produces two very similar pictures — same parabolic 'lens' envelope opening from the left, same fan of arcs on the right, same colours — for roughly the first two thirds of the cycle; the last third diverges (the original ends in a fanned wedge cut by a dark diagonal, the port in a smooth lens over a large dark ellipse).

Divergence within the cycle is in SPATIAL FREQUENCY scheduling, not repertoire. At 16 phase-matched moments of one cycle (ph2-orig / ph2-port, dumped at (10+k/16) x each side's own period), the dominant ramp period per half-strip runs orig 2,15,10,15,6,11,5,5,5,9,13,4,4,4,4,13 vs port 15,13,3,11,13,10,5,5,12,11,2,2,13,7,12,5 — same 2-15 px repertoire, uncorrelated ordering. The block brightness envelope at those same matched phases DOES track (left-half means orig/port 11/9, 97/83, 53/51, 7/6, 13/11, 13/9, 12/8, 10/6, 98/86, 64/71, 79/76).

The original also tends to run BOTH halves at the same ramp period (10/10, 15/15, 6/6, 11/11, 5/5, 13/13, 4/4 at most sampled phases), whereas the port frequently splits them (15/4, 13/8, 10/5, 7/9) — the two blocks drift apart on the port in a way they mostly do not on the original.

Brightness dynamic range differs. Over 120 s the original's frame-mean brightness never exceeds 78 (4 frames above 70, none above 85); the port reaches 143, with 34 frames above 70, 10 above 85 and 2 above 100. Dumping the port at t=34.70-34.85 s shows all 60 pixels at near-full output (peak channel 235-254) — a whole-strip white/saturated wash lasting ~0.15 s. At the phase-matched original moment (t=57.75-58.10 s) the original is at its normal two-block ramp texture, frame mean 37-51. These blowouts recur on the port roughly every 10-25 s (t~6.5, 26.1, 34.8, 89.8, 104.8 s).

Numerically the port carries an extra sub-cycle ripple the original lacks: the original's short-lag brightness autocorrelation decays monotonically and stays flat (lags 1-44 never rise back above 0.11), while the port's oscillates with a ~15.7-frame (0.79 s) period (lag 15 = +0.36, lag 23 = -0.35, lag 31 = +0.22). Scaled by 5/3 that would be a 26-frame ripple on the original, and there is none there.

Average colour balance is close but the port is a touch warmer: over 120 s orig meanR/G/B 37.6/53.6/29.9 vs port 45.9/53.8/25.8 (~22% more red, ~14% less blue). Average overall brightness matches (orig 40.4, port 41.9) and both are brightnessTrend 'steady' with no decay over 120 s.
Control surfaces match: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' on BOTH sides, so there is no dial-surface gap.

Rig behaviour matches: re-rendering both on a 16x16 grid (grid16) leaves each side's stats byte-identical to its strip run (orig mean 40 / motion 13, port mean 42 / motion 22), so both are pure pixel-index patterns and neither gains or loses structure with the rig.
feedback: The single biggest fix: the port's master time base is 5/3 too fast. The original's full animation cycle is 6.55 s (131 frames at 20 fps); the port's is 3.93 s (78.6 frames). Slow the whole animation by a factor of 1.667 and the cycle envelopes line up — the phase offset is already correct (best phase shift is 0 with no adjustment).

After the speed fix, the remaining structural gap is that the port's spatial ramp frequency visits the right values at the wrong times. Both sides sweep ramp periods over the same 2-15 px range across a cycle, but at matched phases they disagree (orig 10 px where the port draws 3 px, orig 4 px where the port draws 13 px). Whatever drives the ramp count should be re-derived from the same phase variable as the brightness envelope, which already matches.

The original keeps both 30 px blocks on the SAME ramp period at almost every moment; the port often runs the two halves at different periods (e.g. 15 px left / 4 px right, 10 px left / 5 px right). Drive the two blocks' ramp frequency from one shared value rather than two independent ones.

Remove the port's whole-strip brightness blowouts. Roughly every 10-25 s the port drives all 60 pixels to near-full output (frame mean up to 143, peak channel 254) for ~0.15 s; the original's frame mean never exceeds 78 and it always keeps some part of the strip dark. This reads as an occasional white flash a viewer would notice.

Related: the port's overall brightness carries an extra ~0.8 s ripple superimposed on the main cycle that the original does not have (visible as an oscillating short-lag autocorrelation). Once the master speed is corrected this sub-oscillation should be checked separately — scaling alone will not remove it.
Minor colour trim: the port averages ~22% more red and ~14% less blue than the original over a full cycle. Overall brightness and green are already right.
